MPI-396 FIXED, committed d5c3d896. Root: uninstall never settled the model's job in the SOT store. THREE compounding defects, all in the card: (1) the REMOTE uninstall leg returns res.json() at downloadManager.js:2410 and never reaches the LOCAL leg's reconciler.reconcileOnce() at :2547 - an engine-split half-wire; (2) pruneTerminal's DONE branch drops on confirmedInstalled.has(id) || age >= DONE_TTL_MS and an uninstalled model is in neither; (3) reconciler.start() gates its tick on store.hasActiveJobs(), so post-uninstall the poll returns early forever and the 120s belt never runs. The stale job was therefore PERMANENT, not transient - which is why Ctrl+R did not clear it (the store is main-process). Fix: store.dropModel(modelId) + broadcastSnapshot() at BOTH legs.

key_decisions: Fixed MPI-396 at the STORE, not at the tile. Suppressing the bar in _tileState when the model is not installed would have left the store reporting a finished job for a model that no longer exists, to the status endpoint and every other snapshot consumer. The user explicitly asked for no more symptom patches on this subsystem - two refactors have already been spent here.

dropModel refuses a NON-terminal job. A model uninstalled mid-download is the uninstall route's in-flight dep guard's business; dropping a live job would strand the transport layer that still owns its downloaders.

Did NOT touch pruneTerminal's TTL policy or the reconciler's hasActiveJobs gate. Both are correct for what they were designed for; the missing piece was that uninstall had no way to speak to the store at all.
Carded MPI-397 and MPI-398 instead of fixing them. MPI-397 needs a product decision (it relaxes the install-state-IS-files-on-disk invariant); MPI-398 needs measurement first.
The negative control keeps one test passing in BOTH states on purpose - it pins that MPI-276's DONE_TTL belt still prunes a job nobody uninstalled.
